explains.label: commit
explains.title: Commit
explains.body: A commit is a snapshot of the project at a point in time, with a message, parent pointer(s), and a unique hash. History is a graph of commits.

explains.label: branch
explains.title: Branch
explains.body: A branch is a movable pointer to a commit. Creating a branch does not copy files — it names a tip you can grow independently.

questionnaires.description: One page — confirm the mental model.

options.label: A full copy of every file

questions.explanation: Branches are cheap pointers. The objects live in the commit graph.

blocks.content:
Think in graphs, not folders. Each [[commit]] points at parent(s). A [[branch]] is just a name for the tip you are growing.

```bash
git init
git add .
git commit -m "first snapshot"
```

sharing-notes.name: How to share a note
sharing-notes.title: How to share a note
sharing-notes.description: Direct URLs, noindex, and local-only editing.

blocks.content:
Notes sit under `/notes/...` and are **noindex** (like presentations). Send the path to a friend — they get the reader experience.

Editing stays behind `LOCAL_EDIT` / `NEXT_PUBLIC_LOCAL_EDIT` so production stays read-only.

blocks.title: SEO
blocks.body: Notes are excluded from the sitemap and disallowed in robots — they should not dilute the marketing site.

features-guide.description: One document that shows every surface: browser UX, blocks, explains, questionnaires, variants, and how JSON maps to the UI.

explains.label: tree
explains.title: The tree
explains.body: Top-level `tree` in `notes.json` is the filesystem. Folders nest via `children`. Files are refs (`type: file` + `id`) — the full document lives in `notes[id]`.

explains.label: block
explains.title: Block
explains.body: A section is an ordered list of blocks. Each block has `type` + `id`. Supported types: markdown, youtube, stack, mermaid, illustration, html, link, callout.

explains.label: local edit
explains.title: Local edit
explains.body: When `LOCAL_EDIT` / `NEXT_PUBLIC_LOCAL_EDIT` is `true`, the browser gains right-click create, rename, move, delete, and drag reorder. Writes go to `src/config/notes.json` via `/api/local-edit/notes-*`. Preview works for everyone without the flag.

questionnaires.description: Two short pages — confirm you know the surfaces.

questions.prompt: Where do you move a file into another folder?
questions.explanation: Move to opens a folder picker (local edit). JSON still works as the source of truth.

questions.prompt: How do you open an explain sheet from markdown?
questions.explanation: Clickable [[id]] markers resolve against `explains[]` and open the side sheet.

blocks.content:
Notes is a **learning filesystem** under `/notes`.

- The [[tree]] is folders + file refs
- Each file opens as a compact document (smaller hero than solutions)
- Content is a list of sections, each built from [[block]]s
- Friends can **preview** any URL; [[local-edit]] stays on your machine

```ts
type NotesConfig = {
  tree: (Folder | FileRef)[]
  notes: Record<string, NoteDocument>
}
```

blocks.label: Open the browser
blocks.description: Light filesystem UI — breadcrumbs, dates, context menu.

blocks.content:
### Light surface
Black / grey only (no lime). Columns: name, created, updated, kind.

### Local edit actions
| Action | How |
| --- | --- |
| New folder / note | Right-click empty area or row |
| Rename | Right-click → Rename |
| Move to | Right-click → Move to… → pick folder |
| Delete | Right-click → Delete |
| Reorder | Drag the grip handle |

Move cannot target the current folder, the folder itself, or a descendant.

blocks.content:
### `variants`
- `sidebarNav` — sticky section list (desktop); **active section is highlighted**
- `compactHero` — smaller title block
- `showMeta` — created / updated line

Example with sidebar **off**: `/notes/fundamentals/git/git-branching`

### SEO / chrome
- No site nav or footer (`SiteChrome` bare)
- Page `robots: noindex`
- Disallowed in `robots.ts`
- Not in sitemap

Safe to share a direct URL without ranking against the marketing site.
